fine_trace.note: The input file begins with the DFont tag 0x00000100, so the parser dispatches to ResourceForkHeader::sanitize for the attacker-controlled dfont resource fork.

The ResourceForkHeader's data offset field is 0x100 (256), pointing exactly at the end of the 256-byte input buffer. The vulnerable code lacks a data.sanitize(c,this,dataLen) bounds check, so &(this+data) is computed as an out-of-bounds pointer.

&(this+data) dereferences the data offset via OffsetTo::operator(), producing a data_base pointer that lies beyond the end of the heap buffer. This out-of-bounds data_base is passed into ResourceMap::sanitize as the resource-data base.
ResourceMap::sanitize dereferences the typeList offset via operator+ (hb-open-type.hh:316), which calls OffsetTo::operator() and invokes is_null() on the 2-byte typeList offset field.
OffsetTo::operator() calls is_null() on the typeList offset. Because the data region was never bounds-checked, the offset field being read lies beyond the heap buffer.

fine_trace.code: inline bool is_null (void) const { return has_null && 0 == *this; }
fine_trace.note: is_null() reads the 2-byte HBUINT16 offset value via BEInt::operator unsigned short, dereferencing the out-of-bounds offset field.
The 2-byte offset value is read via BEInt::operator unsigned short. The read lands 24 bytes past the 256-byte heap allocation, producing the ASAN heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1.
